intent: Replace toy-like tank shapes with distinct realistic military proportions; preserve independent barrel architecture.

prompts.light_tank:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production transparent PIXEL ART tank component sheet for a serious military side-scrolling game.
Art direction: believable real military machinery, NOT a toy, not cute, not cartoon. Exact flat side elevation, front to the RIGHT. Real low wide proportions, thin steel sheet edges, small detailed roadwheels inside deep continuous tracks, muted dusty olive/charcoal camouflage, subtle restrained highlights, readable individual pixels and fine clustered dithering. No thick bright outlines, no balloon roadwheels, no glowing rim, no smooth 3D render. Body width roughly THREE TIMES body height; low flattened turret no taller than one third total body height. Sparse real field equipment, seams, grills, smoke launchers. Only two painted components on genuine transparent background with wide empty gutter:
TOP: COMPLETE hull, tracks, turret and hatches, but NO projecting MAIN CANNON. Small realistic rectangular mantlet/socket at front of turret, not an oversized round socket. Include a tiny visible coaxial machinegun port just beside this attachment.
BOTTOM: detached main cannon along perfectly horizontal axis pointing RIGHT, small breech attachment at LEFT, narrow long steel tube and realistic muzzle at RIGHT. Barrel length roughly 40 percent of hull width, narrow bore; same pixel grid and physical scale as body so parts assemble by translation only.
Generous transparent margins around both components, no shadow, floor, text, measurements, labels or other vehicles. No repeated frames. Keep the realistic silhouette legible at a final body width of about 200 game pixels. Uniform high resolution integer-enlarged pixel art.
Vehicle identity: Light tank inspired by the actual M8 Armored Gun System: very compact low boxy aluminum hull, six SMALL roadwheels, thin track, low wedge turret with angular add-on armor plates, slender105mm cannon. Correct military proportions, not a miniature Abrams. Avoid chubby turret and oversized wheels.
